_comment: OSForge-managed base settings, merged non-destructively into ~/.claude/settings.json by deploy.sh. Top-level keys are authoritative; env is merged key-by-key preserving the user's own env. Keys listed in _unset are REMOVED from the live settings — that is how OSForge retracts a setting it previously pushed. Goal: cut MCP context bloat.
_unset_rationale: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto shipped here as an anti-bloat measure and did the opposite. Per the Claude Code MCP docs, UNSET is the aggressive setting: every MCP tool is deferred and loaded on demand. 'auto' switches to threshold mode, loading schemas UPFRONT whenever they fit within 10% of the context window. Measured on this machine: 11 servers, 32 MCP tools, all loaded at session start, inside a 71-83k token baseline. Removing the key restores full deferral without removing a single MCP server. https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp#configure-tool-search
